chunks: Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf narrated from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said:
Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who guaranteed the person of another man that he should be detained, and he said to him: “Seek your companion.”
And he عليه السلام ruled: “There is no kafalah in a hadd.”

key_terms.بِنَفْسِ رَجُلٍ: for the person or bodily presence of a man
key_terms.تَكَفَّلَ: undertook surety or guarantee for another person
key_terms.صَاحِبَكَ: your companion, meaning the person whose presence was guaranteed
key_terms.كَفَالَةَ: legal surety or guarantee of a person’s presence

ai.seo_question: Is kafalah valid in cases involving hadd punishments in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام concerning kafalah, or guaranteeing the presence of a person. It indicates that in cases involving hadd punishments, such a guarantee is not recognized, and the guarantor is told to produce the person he guaranteed.
